title: Backend mid domain message queues async
topic: Backend mid domain message queues async
question: Why would you put a message queue between two services instead of having one call the other directly, and what do you give up by doing that?
idealAnswer:
Decouples the producer and consumer in time: the producer can keep going even if the consumer is slow or temporarily down, since the message just waits in the queue

Smooths out load spikes, the consumer processes at its own sustainable rate instead of being overwhelmed by a burst of direct calls (buffering/backpressure)

Enables retries and durability: a failed processing attempt can be retried, or sent to a dead-letter queue for inspection, without the original caller needing to know or care

Names the cost: it trades a simple synchronous request/response (caller knows immediately if it worked) for eventual, asynchronous processing, plus the operational overhead of running and monitoring the queue itself

Mentions at-least-once delivery as the common default guarantee, and that consumers therefore need to handle receiving the same message more than once (idempotent processing)
